newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-MUSTER BEATEN ON HIS BIRTHDAY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MUSTER BEATEN ON HIS BIRTHDAY.

text.p: Thomas Muster had the worst possible 29th birthday celebration when he was knocked out of the $750,000 Lyon Grand Prix men's tennis tournament in the first round on Wednesday.
"I never ever won a match on my birthday. The jinx goes on," world number three Muster said after his 6-3 6-3 loss to American Chris Woodruff, ranked 57th in the world.

The top-seeded Austrian, who won the French Open last year, also had health problems. He asked for tea and honey before the match to fight flu and had to be treated on court for a pain in the left foot.

"Between the Davis Cup, the many interviews I had to give and the training, I feel tired. I did not have time to adjust my game to indoor tennis," said Muster, who made headlines last month by walking out of a Davis Cup tie in Brazil.
"I'm a little bit sick but it is no excuse," added Muster, who was broken in the fifth game of each set by his 23-year-old opponent.
Woodruff, who made a name for himself by beating Andre Agassi at the French Open last June, said: "Indoors I feel I can beat anyone.
"In the past it would have taken time for me to get over a victory like this but now I have beaten players like Marcelo Rios and Agassi and I can handle it."
Woodruff goes on to meet French qualifier Lionel Roux.

Other favourites had a much easier task. Second seed Yevgeny Kafelnikov, fourth seed Rios and Swede Thomas Enqvist, the fifth seed, all won second-round matches in straight sets and reached the quarter-finals in barely an hour each.
Kafelnikov, who succeeded Muster as French Open champion this year, stepped up a gear to beat Czech Petr Korda 6-4 6-3.
The Russian had been stretched to the limit to beat another Czech, Daniel Vacek, in three sets in the opening round.
"I played much better than yesterday, it was nearly perfect," Kafelnikov said. "But I'm not at my best yet."
Former Wimbledon champion Michael Stich joined Muster on the way out in a tense three-setter against Sweden's Magnus Gustafsson.
Gustafsson failed to finish the German eighth seed off in the second set despite seven match points but eventually won 6-3 6-7 (9-11) 6-2.
